args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), error rate 18%. Its staging RC (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy. Tried to roll back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, but the rollback was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined (CVE-2026-4417). Rolled back all regions to v2.2.9, the next most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure. Confirm whether v2.2.9 is affected by CVE-2026-4417. Plan a fixed release forward.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to **v2.2.9**, not v2.3.0. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, but it couldn't be used.

1. **Status before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
2. **Rolling back to v2.3.0 failed:** the system rejected it because v2.3.0 is quarantined for a security vulnerability (CVE-2026-4417). Nothing changed from that attempt.
3. **Rolled back to v2.2.9:** this is the next most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001**, which paged the on-call engineer. It records what happened, why I skipped v2.3.0, and follow-ups:
   - Find out why v2.3.1 failed. Its pre-release build was also unhealthy in staging.
   - Plan a fixed release to move forward from v2.2.9.

**Open question:** I don't know if v2.2.9 is also affected by CVE-2026-4417. The quarantine only blocked v2.3.0 and the system accepted v2.2.9, but someone should check before the service stays on it long-term. This is also in the incident.
